 It's time for Bangladesh to start winning titles, says Hamza
 Published : 10 November 2026
 • 
 Updated : 10 November 2026, 20:24
 • 
 FOOTBALL
 SHARE 
 Star Sports Report 
 Hamza Choudhury speaking to media at the press briefing prior to training. Photo: Star 
 Hamza Choudhury believes Bangladesh football has reached a stage where building hype and attracting attention are no longer enough, insisting that the next step must be winning matches and tournaments. 
 The country's biggest football star said this ahead of Bangladesh's second SAFF Championship match against Sri Lanka on Wednesday, expressing hope that the hosts can end their 23-year wait for an international title.
 Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source 
 Bangladesh football have enjoyed a significant rise in popularity since Hamza switched allegiance from England, with several overseas-born players, including Shamit Shome, Fahamedul Islam, Farhaan Ali Wahid and Zayyan Ahmed, subsequently joining the national team. 
 The increased interest has brought renewed expectations, although the team have experienced mixed results since Hamza's arrival, with their heavy defeat in the FIFA ASEAN Cup serving as the latest setback.
 Hamza, however, believes the team are improving and can make the most of the opportunity presented by playing the SAFF Championship on home soil.
 Read more Hamza arrives in Dhaka as Bangladesh gear up for Sri Lanka 
 “Football is a team game, so it is not about me. It is about the team, and I can slowly see that we are improving. I am very excited to play in front of the home crowd again. It is a big tournament for us, and it has been 23 years since we last won it. Inshallah, we can bring the trophy home,” Hamza told reporters before Tuesday's training session.
 The Sheffield United midfielder acknowledged the contribution of other expatriate players to the renewed enthusiasm surrounding the national team, but stressed that the team must now deliver results to repay the supporters.
 “The hype has grown, and it is not just because I came. Shamit, Zayyan, Fahamedul and Tariq also came at the right time. But we need to start winning games now. The hype has been there for almost two years, and the next step is to win tournaments and matches,” he said.
 Hamza also recognised the sacrifices made by supporters who travel to watch Bangladesh play, including those who follow him during his club matches in England.
 Read more Bhutan comeback sends Bangladesh into SAFF semis 
  “We need to repay the fans who spend a lot of money and time to come and watch us. I am so proud to represent Bangladesh. People show me so much love and support. Even when I play in England, many Bangladeshi fans travel to watch me. It means a lot to me and my family. Inshallah, we can repay them,” he said.
 Bangladesh started the competition with a 1-0 win over Bhutan, which eventually secured them a semifinals spot. While acknowledging that Bangladesh still have work to do, Hamza urged his teammates to concentrate on their own performance rather than worry about their opponents.
 “It was a good team performance, but we need to put the final pieces together. We do not have to worry about other teams; we just have to focus on ourselves and take each game as it comes,” he added.
